correctness.rationale: The explicit domain is four independently uniform circle points and the acute angle between diagonals. Dirichlet(1,1,1,1) spacings arise from a distinguished sampled vertex, not an absolute-angle-order anchor. Gamma aggregation supplies independent conditional uniforms. A direct diagonal area identity proves the two-independent-cosine representation, giving exact one-dimensional CDF, moment formulas, support and a fixed-angle half-disk upper-tail coefficient. The standalone Cartesian checker and independent cosine integration were executed; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The target is a joint/conditional law for the area of four i.i.d. circle-boundary points at every fixed acute diagonal angle. The exact earlier angle-only marginal, unconditional inscribed-polygon near-maximum area laws, radial intersection-point laws, and different chord-sampling sine law do not imply the conditional area CDF, its conditional variance, or its support. Historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: Historical literature on joint random-chord angle and quadrilateral-area distributions is not exhaustively accessible.
The closest published cyclic-quadrilateral side-variance result was inspected through its available scientific summary, not full text; its deterministic parameters and claim differ materially.
Earlier 1960s random-chord articles were not available in full and priority is not independently certified.

value.rationale: The joint relation of a canonical shape observable (diagonal angle) and a size observable (area) is a natural full-dimensional statistical question. The exact conditional law at every angle, its support, variance and sharp upper-tail provide substantive information not implied by either marginal or by deterministic diagonal inequalities; it furnishes a natural benchmark for random quadrilateral geometry.
